turns.content: A Klebsiella pneumoniae lawn on Mueller-Hinton agar was tested with an amoxicillin-clavulanate disc placed 25 mm centre-to-centre from erythromycin and then chloramphenicol discs, with no zone distortion. What assay was intended, and which antibiotic class should its indicator discs belong to?

PCR produced bands at the expected sizes for blaCTX-M-1 (950 bp) and blaTEM (1080 bp). What do those bands support, and what identity claims remain limited without controls, sequencing, replication, or independent confirmation?
What culture medium and disc geometry are appropriate for a bacterial double-disc synergy test, and how should the genotypic PCR evidence be interpreted alongside the phenotype?
Which disc substitution would correctly implement a clavulanate double-disc synergy test for extended-spectrum beta-lactamase activity?
Check that the correction changes the indicator antibiotic class while retaining the bacterial susceptibility medium, useful spacing, and separately qualified PCR evidence.
Report the experimental improvement and the evidential status of the two expected-size PCR bands.
